transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I’ve kind of started arranging my life around avoiding elevators. Like, I’ll take five flights of stairs at home instead, and I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I’ve even stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another way up. It’s getting inconvenient, and I figured I should talk to someone about it.
What is it about elevators that scares you most?

It’s mostly the thought of getting stuck, or the elevator suddenly dropping. I know, logically, an office elevator is probably safe. But when I see the older doors in my apartment building or at work, my brain just reacts like I’m about to be trapped in there, even though part of me knows that’s kind of over the top.
Do you get that surge of fear only when you’re in or about to use an elevator?

Yeah, pretty much. It hits right when I’m about to use one—like if I step toward the elevator or hear it clunk open. My chest tightens, my hands get sweaty, and I get this sudden rush of panic before I’ve even really thought about it.
Have you ever had that same sudden rush of panic when you were not near an elevator or thinking about using one?
No, not that I’ve noticed. It really seems tied to elevators or being about to use one.
